Just now

WordPress 7.0 shipped a built-in AI Client and a Settings → Connectors screen wired to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google — with no off-switch in the dashboard. The reassuring part: core ships no keys and sends nothing until someone configures a connector. The uncomfortable part: any editor with the right capability can, and stored connector keys are masked but not encrypted.
The fix is a single constant in wp-config.php, placed above the “stop editing” line: define( ‘WP_AI_SUPPORT’, false );. Because it loads before any plugin, it’s enforced in a way the wp_supports_ai filter and disable-AI plugins are not — neither can override it. Verify with wp eval “var_dump( wp_supports_ai() );” and look for bool(false).
There are two boundaries worth knowing before you assume full coverage — one about plugins that bundle their own AI, and one about the Connectors screen itself — plus a small mu-plugin that closes the second gap. The full method comparison, the coverage table, and the mu-plugin code are in the original guide on AHosting.
— Matt Chrust, Director of Business Development, AHosting
